result.reason: The operative language meets the fallback position: affiliates are covered without even requiring notice, and Sparkling may transfer the licence in an M&A transaction. It also adds the preferred contractor coverage. However, it does not achieve the full preferred position because it omits perpetual and irrevocable treatment for paid-up licences and uncured-material-breach protection for subscription licences. The amendment is not minimal and does not preserve unrelated intent because Section 20(d) also gives Garman a new consent-free M&A assignment right, despite the playbook requiring successor transferability only for the Customer; the margin comment incorrectly states that the remaining consent requirements are unchanged.
